Just because it isn't harmful doesn't make it okay. I'm against it. That data is mine, no one has a right to see it but me.

I'm against everyone that wants to "take a piece of me". It isn't right.

But people see things about you all the time. They could check your phone in a phonebook, the police could ask for information about you if they are doing an investigation. Companies probably already had their ways of finding what their costumers wanted long before the internet... What has really changed? Do the people that see your data even know who you are? Maybe all they see is that there's a high percentage of people who search for the word "noodles" on google and you are just a number in that percentage.

The difference is I can mitigate most of those if I choose. I can choose to unlist my number, and verify that it is, indeed, unlisted. The police have to have enough cause to get a warrant. I could choose to only use cash and limit what companies could confirm about me.

I don't care that they don't know who I am, I care that I couldn't stop it if I tried. And even if they told me it was stopped, I couldn't verify it. Technology is a necessity to be a part of modern day society, and there should still be a right to privacy in modern society. That right is eroding.

Right I understand... But think with me. Let's say you take the bus everyday and whenever you buy the bus ticket a guy takes notes. He writes all your physical features, your behaviour, where you are and where you are going. He doesn't care about your name or who you are, but he wants this data so he will improve the bus lines, provide better service and, of course, gain more profits with that. How is this situation much different from the data mining? What guarantee do you have that this kind of stuff isn't already being done in many services you use regardless of the internet. I mean I don't like it either but some breaches of privacy can't be avoided and I really wonder if we should be freaking out about it.

Of course, if they start using this data for dangerous stuff.. that's another story. So I think we should be allowed at least to know where our data is being sent and to have the option to not let it be sold or something like that.

The point is, if I DONT want the bus driver to do that, I don't have to take the bus. I can walk, drive, bike, anything. If I don't want to give out my data online, it's much harder to choose a different service that doesn't data mine (aka none) or stop using the Internet. It just isn't possible. It is much easier to mitigate the data people receive about you in non electronic formats. I'm sure it IS done in other places. But you can take steps to prevent it almost anywhere except online, where your only option is abstinence. Which we all know doesn't work.

And the issue with being told what the data is used for is that there is no guarantee. We don't see it. We don't know if it's true. We don't even know what they collected or where it's from. It's the secrecy that isn't right.
